blocks.text: Resuming is the skill that brings together all the B1: understanding a text without vowels, distinguishing the essential from the secondary, rewording with own words, connecting ideas with the Connective. On examination B1 you will write an Arabic summary of an Arabic text of about 250 words, 100–120 words; In real life you will sum up articles, meetings, phone calls. In this unit you learn a method in five steps (understand, choose, delete and generalize, reformulate, link), the formulas typical of the summary ( ⁧يَتَنَاوَلُ النَّصُّ⁩ …, ⁧يَرَى الكَاتِبُ أَنَّ⁩ …, ⁧وَيَخْلُصُ إِلَى أَنَّ⁩ ...) and techniques for shortening: indirect discourse, the maṣdar, the general term. Three weeks.

Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. identify the main idea, the secondary ideas and the conclusion of an argumentative or chronic text;
2. delete examples, quotes, repetitions and secondary details, and replace lists by a general term;
3. Reword with indirect discourse ( ⁧أَكَّدَ أَنَّ⁩ ...) and with maṣdar ( ⁧اِرْتِفَاعُ الأَسْعَارِ⁩ );
4. write a summary in Arabic of 100–120 words, neutral and well connected, with the typical formulas;
5. read in silence a text by 200–250 words at least 65–70 words per minute and summarize it.

blocks.text: In the reading tests (and in the work) they will often ask you to summarize an Arabic text in English. The method is the same, with two extra attentions:
1. Do not translate before and summarize after: work directly on ideas, with notes in English on the margins of the Arabic text.

2. Make Arabic formulas with natural Italian formulas: ⁧يَرَى الكَاتِبُ أَنَّ⁩ • according to the author (s); ⁧يُذْكَرُ أَنَّ⁩ Go Recall that it is not possible to use the word "switches' in the form of "switches'. ⁧أَمَّا⁩ … ⁧فَـ⁩ As for... You're taking it back. In the oral summary (Script B, oral production) the rhythm is slower than that of a conversation: pause after the sentence that says the argument, pause before the conclusion.
